3: ## Unreleased
4: 
5: - Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
6: - OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 has taken over the `opencode` command: they find your OpenCode 1 install, and if there isn't one, the task stops straight away and says what to do instead of failing with an unrecognized flag. A worker can also point at a specific OpenCode 1 install.
7: - OpenCode 2 workers work again with OpenCode 2.0 and later, even when that install has also taken over the `opencode` command. Tasks, follow-ups, the model list with its effort levels, and continuing a task in a terminal all work, and a worker can point at a specific OpenCode 2 install.
8: - Picking a task from the list now puts you straight in its reply box.
9: - ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) now shows or hides the task list, and puts you right in it so the arrow keys move between tasks.
10: - The reply box is simpler: task details and options now live behind the + button, so typing your next message is the only thing in the way.
11: - Settings can now pick the worker for you: turn on Choosing a worker, paste your TypeSafe key, and work you hand over without naming a worker lands on the one whose strengths fit what you asked for. Your own rules still catch anything it can't answer, and the task shows which worker was suggested and whether the work went there.
12: - Claude workers can now run newer models, like Opus 5.5, by using the Claude Code already installed on your machine instead of the older copy Oga shipped with.
13: - A task no longer fails with a confusing error when it starts just as Oga itself is starting up.
14: - The reply box no longer jumps when the note about continuing a paused task appears, and that note now lines up with the options under the box.
15: - Text in a task's activity log — command output, labels, and the response — now reads at one consistent size instead of jumping between sizes.
16: 
17: ## 0.2.1 - 2026-09-21
18: 
19: - The Charts view in the usage window now works. It shows cost and tokens day by day for the month you are on, and the month arrows move the charts as well as the grid. Both now fill the window instead of sitting in a narrow strip down the middle.
20: - A task no longer ends as blocked just because the worker said it was stuck. A run that hit a slow test or a missing setup and worked around it now finishes as done, and a task only stops for you when the worker asks a question or the run itself fails.
21: - A worker that never answers when a task starts now gives up in half the time, and the task says what that worker said before it went quiet instead of only that it did not answer.
22: 
23: - Settings now lists every keyboard shortcut in one place, grouped by what you are doing, so you can look up what to press without hunting through tooltips.
24: 
25: - You can now send work to fx, alongside Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, and Pi. Pick it in Settings and choose from the models your fx account can reach.
26: - You can now send work to Cursor. Sign in to Cursor once from your terminal, then pick it in Settings and choose from the models your account can reach.
27: - Workers in Settings now open as their own page instead of unfolding inside the list, so the form, the models, and the environment have room to read. The window also uses the full height of your screen.
28: - Worker messages in the task timeline now show their formatting — bold, code, lists — instead of the raw symbols.
29: - An instruction you send a Claude or OpenCode worker while it works now reaches it straight away, instead of waiting for the current run to end. Other workers still pick it up the moment that run finishes.
30: - Each step a worker takes now shows as one row that expands to its result, grouped under the turn it ran in; repeated or renamed steps no longer split into duplicates, and worker logs stay out of the way.
31: - Answers you send a worker now appear in full in the transcript instead of stopping mid-sentence.
32: - "Show more" on a long request now opens the whole thing; it used to stop part way with no way to read the rest.
33: - Changed files now let you pick what you are looking at: this run's edits, everything not yet committed, or the checkout compared with any branch you choose.
34: - Code questions now answer with up to seven places instead of ten.
35: - A task whose model is unavailable or rate limited now says so on one row, with the attempt it is on, instead of a run of rows that say nothing. When the worker gives up because it ran out of usage, the task waits for that to reset and carries on by itself instead of ending with an error.
36: - The task list keeps every task's status right on its own. A task that finished no longer slips back to looking like it is still working, and the list catches up by itself after a connection drop, so you never have to refresh to trust what it says.
37: 
38: ## 0.2.0 - 2026-09-13
39: 
40: - Code questions no longer answer from files your git setup ignores, such as local notes and reports.
41: - Code questions with several words now leave out files that only share one everyday word with them.
42: - Code questions answer faster; the first question after updating rebuilds the project's index once.
43: - You can now point a code question at one folder or file, so the answer only comes from there.
44: - A task's details now show the branch its checkout is on right now, not the one it started with. The details row also stays tidy when you zoom the app.
45: - Starting a task no longer freezes the app or other running tasks. Oga now writes its records and reads your shell setup off the main path, and keeps its database log from growing without limit.
46: - Tasks now stay responsive while Oga prepares or removes large separate checkouts in the background.
47: - Dozens of small polish fixes across the app: waiting tasks show a fine dashed ring, buttons no longer double-submit, stopping a task always asks first, truncated paths show the full name on hover, settings and usage speak in plain words instead of internal names, and dialogs keep your focus while you type.
48: - Changed files now open full screen, with the file list beside the diffs so you can read a task's whole change end to end.
49: - The red connection bar no longer flashes across the top every time a new task lands. It now shows only when Oga is really unreachable.
50: - Each code answer now says in a few words what the match is, so you can pick the right one without opening it.
51: - Repeated code questions answer almost at once, since the project is not re-scanned each time.
52: 
53: ## 0.1.0 - 2026-09-10
54: 
55: - Replies, briefs and update notes now show tables, checklists, crossed-out words, dividers, and lists inside lists, instead of the raw symbols they were written with.
56: - Underlined titles now read as titles, links written as references resolve, spelled-out punctuation shows the real character, and a star or bracket meant literally stays on the page instead of formatting the words around it.
57: - Long replies now appear the moment you open them. A reply with several paragraphs of plain prose used to take a visible pause to draw.
58: - Changes now read the way they do in your editor: full colour in every language, the exact words that changed picked out inside a line, and line numbers on what came from the checkout. Both the changed files panel and the diffs inside activity get it, and the Unified and Split choice still holds.
59: - Activity rows now name work done through Oga in plain language and show concise results when you expand them, instead of exposing technical tool names or raw response data.
60: - Work you hand off now carries a brief the size of the job. A one-line request stays one line, instead of being padded out with headings and numbered steps it doesn't need.
61: - Sorting the task list by priority now puts failed, cancelled, and blocked tasks near the top, where they need you, instead of burying them at the bottom with the finished ones.
62: - You can now set the rules your agent follows when it writes up work to hand off — for one project or for all of them — under Settings ▸ Brief Rules.
63: - Opening the app no longer replays old notifications and activity you had already seen before you last closed it.
64: - `oga query` now takes a path, or `path#name`, and answers with that exact place. It also finds two-letter names like `db`, and no longer lets something you taught it with `oga relearn` come ahead of the name you typed.

90: ## 0.0.8 - 2026-09-07
91: 
92: ### Removed
93:

95: 
96: ### Changed
97: 
98: - Which model a delegated task lands on is decided by `kind` and a loved rule, never a hardness score. `kind` gains a `ux` subject alongside the existing ones.

100: 
101: ### Fixed
102: 
103: - `oga love <model> --when general` now takes every piece of work no other rule claimed, instead of only the work Oga reads as nothing in particular. A rule naming the task's subject or class still wins, and a rule with no `--when` at all still catches whatever is left.
104: - The Usage activity grid is now a compact, centred strip with weekday labels aligned to its rows.
105: - `oga query` now returns every strong match, ranked, instead of collapsing to one arbitrary pick when a word was taught as a hint for several unrelated places. Adding or dropping a word no longer flips the answer between unrelated files for no visible reason.

107: ## 0.0.7 - 2026-09-06
108: 
109: ### Added
110: 
111: - Release manifests now include the release notes shown in the update prompt.
112: - `oga love --when` now routes by subject as well as class: `oga love opencode:muse --when ui` sends UI work there, with `backend`, `database`, `docs`, `tests`, `review`, `research`, and `refactor` alongside the existing kinds. A subject rule wins over a class rule, and `oga delegate --kind <subject>` names the subject when the task text never says so.
113: - `--kind` now also names a class of work — `mechanical`, `general`, `build`, `context`, `reasoning` — not just a subject, so a coding agent that already knows the work is, say, mechanical or a build reaches its loved model for that kind even when the brief itself reads like something else.
114: - `oga love` now takes an ordered list of destinations per rule, like `oga love opencode:luna:max claude:opus:low --when ui`. The first destination that can take the work runs it; when it is rate-limited, out of credits, or otherwise unavailable, the next one runs instead, and the task record says which one ran and why it was not the first. Each destination is `worker:model:effort` with the model or the effort left out.
115: - Work a delegated worker ships now says which worker, model, and effort produced it, credited on the commits it makes. Turn it off per project with `worker: attribution: false` in `.oga.yaml`, or everywhere with the same key in `~/.oga.yaml`.
116: - `oga archive --delete-branch` can now remove a worktree task's local branch safely, while explaining when Git keeps it.
117: - The Usage window can now switch its activity view between the month grid and charts: cost and tokens over the selected range, plus a cost-by-model breakdown. The grid stays the default.
118: 
119: ### Removed
120: 
121: - The project map is gone. Asking `oga query` a question in plain language points at the exact line, so browsing a generated listing no longer has a place. Anything the old map kept is cleaned up the first time this version runs, and a worker prompt that mentioned it keeps working.
122:

125: - The worker's default habits — clearing small reversible obstacles itself, looking code up with `oga query` first, and delivering through checks, a commit, and a pull request — moved out of the app into the worker rules you can rewrite or delete in Settings. If you already customized your rules, they stay exactly as you left them.
126: - The worker prompt is now plain text you own top to bottom: reorder the sections, rewrite one, or drop one. Nothing is appended behind your back, and a prompt you had already customized keeps working.

132: - Looking something up returns in milliseconds, and a project you have not touched is ready again almost instantly.
133: - The task footer now shows how full the worker's context is, and how far it has grown since the run started.

## TL;DR

- Three read-only subagents surveyed the repository in parallel.
- No files were changed; no builds or tests were run.
- Results came from real file listing, reading, and grep calls.

## A — Rust crates

- `oga-acp`: Agent Client Protocol transport, permissions, sessions, and outcomes.
- `oga-advisor`: Selects a connected worker and effort level from a task brief.
- `oga-client`: Typed broker access, event streams, and client bridges.
- `oga-config`: Profiles, layered YAML configuration, project settings, models, and prompts.
- `oga-context`: Tree-sitter project index behind `oga query` and `oga relearn`.
- `oga-domain`: Shared domain types and serialization conventions.
- `oga-events`: Task event normalization, persistence, streaming, and observation.
- `oga-http`: Axum HTTP routes for broker state, settings, usage, discovery, and actions.
- `oga-mcp`: Stateless MCP/JSON-RPC server for task management and discovery.
- `oga-pricing`: Model facts, pricing data, caching, and spend estimates.
- `oga-providers`: Provider commands, sessions, transcripts, events, and usage parsing.
- `oga-routing`: Task classification and provider/model/effort routing policy.
- `oga-runner`: Provider process execution, cancellation, timeouts, and confinement.
- `oga-service`: Task dispatch, lifecycle, dependencies, holds, deliveries, and worker runs.
- `oga-store`: SQLite persistence, schema, repositories, connections, and writes.
- `oga-worktree`: Git worktree and branch creation, checkout, cleanup, joining, and diffs.

## B — `web/src/domain/activity/`

- `index.ts`: Activity and handoff types; composition, query, normalization, projection, and narration APIs; exported activity-title constants.
- `acp.test.ts`: No exports; tests ACP folding, deduplication, streaming, and recorded runs.
- `index.test.ts`: No exports; tests composition, handoffs, subagents, projection caching, streams, and narration.
- `fixtures/claude-acp-resumed.json`: Recorded Claude ACP event rows; no code exports.
- `fixtures/probe-rows.json`: Recorded event-row arrays; no code exports.
- `fixtures/antigravity-acp-probe.json`: Recorded Antigravity event rows; no code exports.
- `fixtures/antigravity-run.jsonl`: Raw Antigravity JSONL trace; no code exports.

## C — `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased

- Settings are roomier and easier to scan, with grouped sections, clear titles, and controls on their own rows.
- OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 owns the `opencode` command, with clear failure guidance and install selection.
- OpenCode 2 workers work with OpenCode 2.0 and later, including models, follow-ups, and terminal continuation.
- Picking a task now puts you directly in its reply box.
- ⌘B/Ctrl+B shows or hides the task list and focuses it.
- The reply box hides details and options behind the + button.
- Settings can choose a worker automatically using a TypeSafe key and matching worker strengths.
- Claude workers can use newer models through the locally installed Claude Code.
- Tasks no longer fail with a confusing startup error.
- The reply box no longer jumps when a paused-task notice appears.
- Task activity text uses one consistent size.

I used the native `functions.subagent` tool; all three subagents ran in parallel. They could not run `oga query` because their child sessions had no shell or query command, but each used real read/list/grep calls.
